clue.text: Tristram bids Andrew be silent

parts.note: 'sh!' is the sound used to tell someone to be silent
Andy is the usual short form of the name Andrew

explanation.surface: A man called Tristram tells his friend Andrew to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bids' is a link: Andrew is told 'Sh!', and the pieces are written with the hush first.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne's comic novel is about Tristram Shandy, so the surname completes the hero's name.

clue.text: One with a crownor four, once

definitions.meaning: an old gold coin worth twenty shillings, four crowns of five shillings

explanation.surface: A ruler with a crown, or four of them in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: In old British money a crown was five shillings, so four crowns made the twenty-shilling gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A reigning monarch, and the old pound coin worth four five-shilling crowns.

clue.text: Movement to "banish Miltonic melancholy

definitions.meaning: a fast section of a symphony or sonata
Milton's poem L'Allegro opens by sending 'loathed Melancholy' away

explanation.surface: A piece of music meant to drive off a gloomy poet's mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk musical section, and Milton's cheerful poem that dismisses gloom in its opening lines.

clue.text: Disapprove of including one showing lower worth

indicators.note: 'including' means the disapprove word holds the one inside it

parts.note: to deprecate is to disapprove of
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes the inclusion of anything that seems to cheapen value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is a link; I goes into DEPRECATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall in value or reduce in price is to lessen worth.

clue.text: Cold in the sea, returning for Thetis's son

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the cold word sits inside the sea word
returning means the word sea is read backwards before the cold goes in

parts.note: taken as written
a chill is a cold, as in catching a chill

explanation.surface: A chill in the sea on the way back for the sea-nymph's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SEA into AES, and CHILL goes inside it after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the sea-nymph Thetis was mother of the hero of the Trojan War, dipped in the Styx.

clue.text: Foolish fellow in company with cautious bird

indicators.note: 'in' puts the foolish fellow inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: an ass is a fool
wary means cautious

explanation.surface: A silly man keeps company with a careful bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless Australasian runner related to the emu is the bird meant.

clue.text: A single Spanish frontier town

parts.note: A means one, and one is the Roman numeral I
a single in cricket is one run

explanation.surface: One lone town on the Spanish border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' is a cricket term for one run scored.
explanation.definitionFit: This Basque town sits on the Bidasoa river, the border crossing into France.

clue.text: Tall fee for revising tract

indicators.note: letters to be revised are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An outrageous charge for editing a pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for revising' rearranges the letters of TALL FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short printed pamphlet handed out is a tract.

clue.text: One goes to it nightly

parts.note: something everyone goes to each night, like an appointment, read as the state of rest

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'go to sleep' makes the restful state a place one goes every night.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to bed and resting each night is the nightly destination.

clue.text: Anagram X — sur la piste

indicators.note: the word itself says the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: an X in a letter stands for a kiss

explanation.surface: A rearranged kiss on the ski slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sur la piste' is French for on the ski run; X written at a letter's end means a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Long runners strapped to boots are what one wears on a ski slope.

clue.text: Tongue for all a turn-up among German people

indicators.note: 'among' places the turned piece inside the word for German people

parts.note: Volk is the German word for people or nation
the letter A followed by 'up' turned over, giving PU

explanation.surface: A universal language arises among the people of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-up' turns UP into PU, set after A to give APU, which goes inside VOLK.
explanation.definitionFit: This invented language of the 1870s was meant as a universal speech that everyone could share.

clue.text: Wear for a priest, dismissed — insane!

indicators.note: 'in' puts the word for dismissed inside the word sane

parts.note: taken as written
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A priest's garment, and the poor fellow sacked and gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'insane' must be read as 'in sane': OUT goes inside SANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassock worn by Roman Catholic clergy is the garment meant.

clue.text: Engineers take vessel in area of retreat

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the engineers and vessel sit inside the area word

parts.note: a region is an area
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
SS, steamship, stands for a vessel

explanation.surface: Army engineers take a ship into an area to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a link; RE + SS make RESS, which goes inside REGION after REG.
explanation.definitionFit: Going backwards to an earlier state is a retreat, a backward movement.

clue.text: Fielder's mistake

definitions.meaning: in cricket a fielder stands at ... beside the wicketkeeper
a small error, as in a ... of the tongue

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one fielder's error, but the two words define separately; slip is a cricket position.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielding position next to the wicketkeeper, and a minor blunder or lapse.

clue.text: Wherein would-be progressive party needs arms for revolution

definitions.text: Wherein would-be progressive party needs arms for revolution

parts.words: Wherein would-be progressive party needs arms for revolution
parts.note: a political party wanting armed revolution, read as a seat with armrests in which a disabled person moves forward by turning wheels

explanation.surface: A reforming party needs weapons to overthrow the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'progressive' means moving forward, 'party' a person, 'arms' armrests and 'revolution' turning wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat on wheels for a person who cannot walk, with armrests and turning wheels.

clue.text: Pressing engagement for which one had to dash away

definitions.text: Pressing engagement for which one had to dash away

parts.words: Pressing engagement for which one had to dash away
parts.note: an urgent appointment that forces one to rush off, read as a session of flattening clothes with a hot iron

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off to an urgent appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' means urgent in the surface but refers to pressing clothes; the household chore is the classic excuse for leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing laundry flat with a hot iron is the household task an excuse-maker claims as an engagement.

clue.text: Assurance of money return malcontents enjoy ?

definitions.text: Assurance of money return malcontents enjoy ?

parts.words: Assurance of money return malcontents enjoy ?
parts.note: a promise of a refund if dissatisfied, which unhappy customers are glad to use

explanation.surface: Grumbling customers like a promise that their cash comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: Shops offer 'satisfaction or your money back', so the discontented benefit from the promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm promise, as in a money-back pledge to dissatisfied buyers.

clue.text: A little talk points to a faithful friend

parts.note: a chat is a short informal talk
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A brief conversation shows a loyal companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points are a crossword staple for single letters N, S, E, W.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's Aeneid, the hero's loyal companion became a byword for a trusty friend.

clue.text: Making one 23 Dn in the South of France or if over one hundred

parts.note: sud is French for south
taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Being over a hundred degrees on the Riviera makes one perspire.
explanation.walkthrough: '23 Dn' refers to the answer of 23 down, perspiration; 'in' and 'over' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for a drug that causes perspiration.

clue.text: Herbert enters. Northern Territory with big guns for oil

indicators.note: 'enters' puts the Herbert piece inside the Territory abbreviation

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for Australia's Northern Territory
A. P. Herbert, the humorist and MP, was known by his initials
HA stands for heavy artillery, big guns

explanation.surface: A man named Herbert arrives in the Australian outback with artillery, hunting for oil.
explanation.walkthrough: A. P. Herbert was a famous Punch humorist and MP, so 'Herbert' gives his initials APH.
explanation.definitionFit: A flammable liquid distilled from petroleum or coal tar is a kind of oil.

clue.text: Moonshine in Ireland

parts.note: illicitly distilled spirits, as made in rural Ireland

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moonshine' here is illicit liquor, not moonlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal home-distilled Irish spirit is the local word for bootleg liquor.

clue.text: The principal income Edward gave up

parts.note: the return earned on a capital sum, or principal, is its yield
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward handed over the main earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' looks like 'main' but is the capital sum on which interest is earned.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender or concede something is to give it up.

clue.text: Tried to. build place in Michigan

indicators.note: build means put the letters together in a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Attempted to construct a town in the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'build' rearranges the letters of TRIED TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The motor city is the largest city in the state of Michigan.

clue.text: David's ancestor from the South.

indicators.note: 'from' signals that letters are made from the word the, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: King David's forebear came up from the southern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is the anagram signal: THE is rearranged to ETH and placed after S.
explanation.definitionFit: In biblical genealogies, Adam's third son heads the line that leads down to King David.

clue.text: Old soldier's outcome of honest toil

definitions.meaning: British slang for a veteran soldier

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier's reward for honest work.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran soldier in British slang, and the perspiration that hard work produces.

clue.text: His stories-stuff with a nonsense backing ?

definitions.text: His stories-stuff with a nonsense backing ?

parts.note: fabric is cloth, or stuff

indicators.note: 'backing' says the nonsense word runs back to front

parts.note: rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: A teller of tall tales spins material with rubbish behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ROT into TOR, placed after FABRIC and A; the whole clue describes a liar.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes up stories is an inventor of falsehoods, a liar.

clue.text: Like a binder that's substandard

definitions.meaning: resembling a cord used to tie things
poor quality, in British informal use

explanation.surface: Like a binding cord that is of poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringy like cord, and British slang for shoddy or poor.

clue.text: Singer or swimmer

definitions.meaning: a male singer with the lowest voice

explanation.surface: A vocalist or a swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The deepest male voice, and a spiny-finned fish.

clue.text: Stylish and French, without an awkward angle

indicators.note: 'without' means outside, so the French word wraps the rearranged letters

parts.note: et is the French word for and

indicators.note: awkward signals the letters of angle are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Smart and French, avoiding any clumsy angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside; 'awkward' rearranges ANGLE to LEGAN, which goes inside ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful and refined in appearance is what stylish means.

clue.text: End-of-run notice to decide the ultimate winner.

definitions.meaning: a show at the end of its run is taken off, a theatre notice
an extra match held to settle who wins

explanation.surface: A notice going up at the end of a season to settle the champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama being taken off stage, and a deciding extra match between leading contenders.

clue.text: Light metal

parts.note: not a metal of low weight but the heavy metal used for filaments in light bulbs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' suggests low weight, but this is a very heavy metal; it gives light as a bulb filament.
explanation.definitionFit: This dense element is used for the glowing filaments of electric lamps.

clue.text: First-nighter at this. Sheridan play ?

definitions.meaning: a reviewer who attends opening nights
Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote a 1779 comedy with this title

explanation.surface: A reviewer attends the opening night of a Sheridan comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer at an opening performance, and the title of Sheridan's burlesque comedy about theatre.
